entries.title: Titus 2:1
segments: The sound doctrine. The very simplicity of faith in Christ seems to have been a stumbling block to the Jews, accustomed as they were to an elaborate ritual.  Perhaps it was for this reason that so many 'teachers' flourished, each trying to establish a system of Christianity embodying his own imaginations.  See

entries.title: Titus 2:8
segments: To say of us. Paul's exhortation to give due regard to the opinions of the non-Christian people, was to preserve the name of Christ free from any reproach.  In this, Peter was in accord with Paul.  See

entries.title: Titus 2:9
segments: Not gainsaving. The Christian attitude is that of lowliness of mind and loving service.  The apprehension of the truth as it is in Christ did not give the bondservant dominion over his master in the flesh, but inspired him to a more consecrated service, 'as unto the Lord' (

entries.title: Titus 2:11
segments: To all men. This declaration has been accepted as a contradiction of the factional doctrine that only the enlightened would receive salvation.  See
